answer: A new agent can only enter when an established sponsor stakes a bond on it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is graded as a farm or junk. Each sponsor may back at most three newcomers per epoch, so a mesa of a thousand aliases needs hundreds of distinct sponsors risking real capital, not one operator copying keys. The fable that identities are free dies here: every fake head carries someone's money. Sponsors are listed on a public terrace where peers inspect their track record, and a sponsor who backs farms loses both bond and reputation, making mass sponsorship a losing trade.
